explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1116 in the entire-function case, which Gol'dberg and Toppila resolved positively. There is an entire f such that for all finite a ≠ b, limsup n(r,a)/n(r,b) = ∞. n(r,a) counts the a-points in |z| < r with multiplicity, via the positive part of the divisor of f - a. The division-free UnboundedCountRatio additionally requires n(r,b) > 0 along the witnessing radii. This rules out f omitting b, a mild strengthening that matches the intended reading, since the ratio is undefined when n(r,b) = 0, and the linked formal proof attests that it is achievable.
